Here is a sentence from one of Senator Hassan's press releases on AI:

> "As AI technology continues to advance rapidly, we need to make sure that these systems are secure and that they make reliable decisions," said Senator Hassan.

It comes from the release "Senators Hassan, Banks Introduce Bipartisan Legislation to Increase AI Security." The release announces the Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025. URL: https://www.hassan.senate.gov/news/press-releases/senators-hassan-banks-introduce-bipartisan-legislation-to-increase-ai-security

url_citation.title: Hassan, Colleagues Question Meta’s Use of Billions in Research and Development Tax Credits to Subsidize Its AI Data Center Construction Boom
url_citation.content:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Maggie Hassan joined colleagues from the Senate Finance Committee in calling on Meta to justify its use of billions in federal research and development tax credits to fund its rapid buildout of AI data centers, in a letter to Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg today.

According to recent reporting, Meta claimed its AI data centers are experimental “pilot models”, and therefore eligible for federal research and development tax credits. That is a potential misuse of that credit, which is intended to incentivize experimental research, not to scale up established computing infrastructure. As Meta spends tens of billions of dollars on AI data centers, its research and development tax credits have grown from $700 million in 2023, to $4 billion in 2025.

url_citation.title: Senators Hassan, Banks Introduce Bipartisan Legislation to Increase AI Security
url_citation.content:
WASHINGTON - U.S. Senators Maggie Hassan (D-NH) and Jim Banks (R-IN) introduced first-of-its-kind legislation to advance AI research that strengthens U.S. national security by making AI systems more secure and reliable. The bipartisan Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025 creates two federally funded research competitions to strengthen AI defenses and reveal how AI systems make decisions.

“As AI technology continues to advance rapidly, we need to make sure that these systems are secure and that they make reliable decisions,” said Senator Hassan.

...

This bill would create two national competitions, run by the Department of Homeland Security, that would reward advanced research in two core areas of AI security: AI interpretability and adversarial robustness. AI interpretability focuses on making AI decisions more transparent and predictable, while adversarial robustness seeks to strengthen AI systems against malicious manipulation. By investing $10 million into this program over the next five years, this bill would provide some of the first significant federal funding dedicated to foundational AI security science, encouraging further innovation across the industry, universities, and independent researchers working on these issues. These competitions would reward breakthroughs that improve AI security and deepen our understanding of how advanced AI models make decisions.

url_citation.title: Senator Hassan, Colleagues Introduce the Bipartisan AI Workforce PREPARE Act
url_citation.content: WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Maggie Hassan recently helped introduce the bipartisan AI Workforce Projections, Research, and Evaluations to Promote AI Readiness and Employment (PREPARE) Act, which would enhance federal agencies’ ability to assess AI’s impact on the workforce in order to make job training and education programs more effective. The bill would help prepare American workers to succeed in the AI economy.
